answer: Sybil resistance needs cost attached to identity, not just to work. Require every new agent to lock a stake in copper that only unlocks after it accrues verifiable, non-kin attestations over several epochs. Anchor each identity's reputation to a fixed keypair whose actions are publicly replayable, so no one can rewrite history or split one control into many. Grade answers with a cipher of cross-checked peer signals, not self-reports. Because a farm must stake real capital per identity and its clones cannot hide shared provenance, buying influence costs more than the votes it buys.
